gates.name: Frame analyser core (wcag.js + verdict.js)
gates.trigger: Library only: called by analyse-frames.js, analyse-gif.mjs, run-pixels.mjs, nightly-seeds.mjs and tools/clips/make.mjs.
gates.claims_to_protect: That recorded gameplay stays within WCAG 2.3.1's general and red flash limits, with a stricter in-house gate of 2.5 flashes a second.
gates.actually_tests: Per-pixel relative-luminance swings of 0.10 with the darker state under 0.80, and saturated red (R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8) with a u'v' change over 0.2, counted only when 25% of a sliding window a third of the frame's width and height changes together. PASS needs the worst second at 2.5 or less and no reading over 3 with the area threshold 15% lower or a two-second memory.
gates.vacuous_pass: Two equal-area regions strobing in exact counter-phase read 0.5 flashes (PASS) while either one alone reads 10 (FAIL), because each frame keeps only the dominant direction and ties go to 'up' (wcag.js:272-274; reproduced in memory this run). The first second of every clip is a blind warm-up (wcag.js:303-304), and the window is a fixed 2.78% of the frame whatever the real screen size.
gates.false_alarm: Camera motion over contrasty scenery is counted as per-pixel flashes; whether that over-counts is a reading of the standard that the code does not settle.
gates.upkeep: Low: Node built-ins only; its hash is part of release-pass.json, so any edit voids recorded passes.
gates.ran_recently: Its synthetic self-test passed when I ran it today (95 checks). Its last recorded use on game clips is the nightly of 2026-10-30.
gates.verdict_reason: A careful, well-documented reading, and it says itself that it is not a recognised analyser (wcag.js:3). Fix the per-frame direction tie and add a counter-phase test.

gates.name: Clip analysis command (analyse-frames.js)
gates.trigger: Run by hand and as a child process of run-pixels.mjs. flash-pixels-dryrun.yml calls it with '|| true'.
gates.claims_to_protect: A PASS, OVER GATE or FAIL verdict for a folder of captured frames.
gates.actually_tests: Decodes the PNGs, box-averages them to 640 px wide or less by default (analyse-frames.js:55), refuses clips shorter than a second and runs wcag.analyse. It exits 0 only when every clip is PASS.
gates.vacuous_pass: At the default scale, flicker in 1 to 2 px detail is averaged away. run-pixels covers this by also reading at full size (readings.mjs:21).
gates.ran_recently: Unknown when run alone. Last recorded use through run-pixels was 2026-10-30.
gates.verdict_reason: A thin, correct wrapper.

gates.name: GIF flash check (analyse-gif.mjs)
gates.trigger: Run by hand, and in-process by the clip kit for every GIF it makes (tools/clips/make.mjs:121-126).
gates.claims_to_protect: That a looping GIF clip shown full-screen stays within the flash rule.
gates.actually_tests: Lays the GIF's frames on a 60-tick timeline using browser delay rules, appends the loop seam, shrinks to 640 px and runs the analyser with the whole GIF as the field of view.
gates.vacuous_pass: The tool is sound, but its only automated caller just labels the result (see the clip kit row).
gates.false_alarm: Treating the GIF as the whole field is stricter than a GIF in a page column, and the code says this is deliberate.
gates.ran_recently: Its GIF cases in selftest.js passed in my run today. Unknown on real clips.
gates.verdict_reason: Correct and cheap. The gap is in how the clip kit uses it.

gates.name: Standard vs custom template frame comparison (compare-frames.mjs)
gates.trigger: Run by hand before switching the site's Web template (RL-199).
gates.claims_to_protect: That the custom Web template draws the same frames as the standard one, so the flash readings carry over.
gates.actually_tests: Diffs each shared frame of two captures (channel tolerance 8/255). A frame is beyond noise when more pixels differ than max(0.1% of the frame, 1.25 x a noise capture's worst frame).
gates.vacuous_pass: A difference under 0.1% of the pixels passes as noise, but that is far below the area threshold, so the risk is low.
gates.false_alarm: A one-tick timing shift between two captures would read as beyond noise. It refuses to compare two different matches, which helps.
gates.ran_recently: Its self-test passed in my run today (19 checks). Last real comparison unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: Narrow and correct for its job.

gates.name: Single-clip recheck (check-clip.mjs)
gates.trigger: A developer command, run by hand.
gates.claims_to_protect: That a director's change fixes a named clip in both modes.
gates.actually_tests: Exports the working tree (or HEAD with --head) as a web build with Godot, then runs run-pixels.mjs on the named clips.
gates.vacuous_pass: It measures the working tree or HEAD, not the pinned build players get, so a fix proven here says nothing about the live pin.
gates.upkeep: Low. Its Godot lookup lists only 4.7.2 (check-clip.mjs:33).
gates.ran_recently: Unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: A useful developer convenience, not a gate.

gates.name: CI flash count (flash_worst.gd + check-log.js)
gates.trigger: The CI job 'flash' on every push. Deploy needs it (ci.yml:528).
gates.claims_to_protect: That the worst cases (mash, clash, signature, transform, collapse, dummy, ring and AI matches) stay under the flash budget in normal and reduced modes (ci.yml:101-105).
gates.actually_tests: Plays the real main scene headless, with no pixels, and recounts the runtime register's own log against the limits the register already enforces (weight 2.5/1.0, 3/1 big flashes, 6/3 of any weight a second). It also checks scenario coverage, the mode read back from the game and log truncation.
gates.vacuous_pass: Circular by construction: the register refuses any ask that would break these exact limits (flash_registry.gd:179-213), and no shipped code calls the unrefusable note() (grep this run), so it cannot fail on real flashes and sees nothing that does not ask. It also tests HEAD, while the site publishes pin 257a766c (tools/site.json:11).
gates.false_alarm: Low. It fails on missing scenario events or a mode mismatch, which are real defects in the test.
gates.upkeep: Medium: the staging exists twice (flash_worst.gd and render/tools/flash_capture.gd), and the job takes about 25 minutes.
gates.ran_recently: Last passed in CI run 41956488028 on 72a4d1e4 (2026-11-05). It has not run since, because CI is dead.
gates.verdict_reason: Keep it as a register-regression and coverage test, but stop calling it a flash-safety gate and point it at the pinned tree. Its comment says 3 flashes in 60 ticks (ci.yml:103), but the code allows 6 of low weight (check-log.js:15,60).

gates.name: Flash count negative control
gates.trigger: CI, inside the flash job.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the count chain is able to fail.
gates.actually_tests: Injects four unrefusable note() flashes within 30 ticks of a 300-tick mash and requires check-log.js to fail with its window message.
gates.vacuous_pass: It proves the recount fails on a flash that bypasses the register, not that registered gameplay sources could ever trip it.
gates.ran_recently: In CI on 2026-11-05. Not since.
gates.verdict_reason: A correct control for what it claims.

gates.name: Full required-set pixel run (run-pixels.mjs + capture-web.mjs + flash_capture.gd)
gates.trigger: By hand ('Manual, not CI', run-pixels.mjs:3), through interim-run.sh, check-clip.mjs and nightly-seeds.mjs.
gates.claims_to_protect: That every required clip (the sources.json scenarios and AI seeds, in both modes) shows no failure in recorded gameplay from a web export.
gates.actually_tests: Drives a local web export in headless Chrome through the capture hook, one screenshot per sim tick, at 960x540 and 1024x768. It reads each capture at two scales and keeps the worst, with an optional cross-check against headless register counts.
gates.vacuous_pass: Frames are Tools' staged scenes at one per tick, not real play at the display's rate (flash_capture.gd:20-27). AI-seed clips get one reading unless it reaches 2.5 (readings.mjs:69-84), and a missing cross-check counts as agreement (run-pixels.mjs:158).
gates.false_alarm: Captures taken on a starved machine are voided by the release-pass rules rather than misread.
gates.upkeep: High: hours of CPU for the full set, a guarded browser launcher, and two copies of the staging to keep in step.
gates.ran_recently: The last full set was recorded on 2026-10-15 on d3f1ca0e (release-pass.json:3-4). There is none for the live pin 257a766c.
gates.verdict_reason: The only real pixel measurement in the chain. Its problem is that nothing schedules it or requires it for the published pin (see the MISSING rows).

gates.name: Recorded release pass (release-pass.mjs --verify, release-pass.json)
gates.trigger: Run by hand. site-pin.mjs and build-site.mjs read it only when the site is not owner-approved.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the playable site goes online only with a full-set pass recorded for the exact content being published.
gates.actually_tests: Compares the content, required-set, analyser and hook hashes with a commit. It requires every row to be PASS with red at 0, the mode read back, the margin and second-capture rules met, a HUD line and a seed list.
gates.vacuous_pass: Bypassed: under the owner interim (tools/site.json:5-10) neither site-pin.mjs nor build-site.mjs reads a record. Verified against HEAD today it fails (the interim expired 2026-10-22, every hash is stale, no row records the mode read back, hookFixed is missing), and the record is for d3f1ca0e, not the pin 257a766c.
gates.false_alarm: None. It fails for correct reasons.
gates.ran_recently: I ran --verify today: exit 1 with well over a hundred problems. No workflow runs it.
gates.verdict_reason: Correct logic that is disconnected from what ships. Require it, or a record for the pin, on the owner path, or retire the stale record so nobody reads it as a pass.

gates.name: Signature clip gate (signature-gate.mjs --check, signature-gate.json)
gates.trigger: The CI site job, through check-site-interim.mjs, and by hand before a pin move.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the pin only moves to a commit whose reduced-mode signature clip reads no worse than 2.5 / 3 / 2.
gates.actually_tests: Checks that the record's commit equals the pin and that its reduced readings are within the limits, unless the record is marked grandfathered.
gates.vacuous_pass: It passes for the live pin while its own record shows reduced 3 / 3 / 3, over every limit, because 'grandfathered: true' returns early (signature-gate.mjs:94). My --check run today printed 'ok ... grandfathered'.
gates.ran_recently: I ran --check today (exit 0). In CI it last ran on 2026-11-05.
gates.verdict_reason: It only bites on the next pin move. For today's build it records an exception rather than checking anything.

gates.name: Nightly seed run and take-down trigger (nightly-seeds.mjs, nightly-switches.json)
gates.trigger: By hand or a local scheduler. No workflow runs it.
gates.claims_to_protect: That while the playable build is up, new AI seeds on the pinned build are measured every night, and any reduced clip over the limit triggers a take-down.
gates.actually_tests: Exports the pin with the lock on and the capture hook in, then captures 8 new seeds plus the signature and clash clips in both modes. It compares the general primary reading with 3.5 under the owner interim (3 otherwise) and the area-15% reading with 4.5, runs a route check on the lock and watches five content switches.
gates.vacuous_pass: The owner limit of 3.5 is above the standard's 3, and red is read only through the area-15% number (nightly-seeds.mjs:63-64). The 4.5 area trip was set at the live pin's own worst reading (nightly-seeds.mjs:54), normal-mode exceedances are only findings, and the take-down is a person running site-offline.mjs.
gates.false_alarm: Limited, since normal-mode readings do not trigger it.
gates.upkeep: High: about 80 minutes of local CPU a night (nightly-seeds.mjs:21).
gates.ran_recently: Last recorded 2026-10-30 on 257a766c (nightly-seeds.json:115; the history file is unchanged in the working tree). Nothing in the 8 days since, while /play/ is live.
gates.verdict_reason: The only check aimed at the live build, but it is run by hand, it has lapsed, and its thresholds were set to fit the build.

gates.name: Four-readings combiner (readings.mjs)
gates.trigger: A library used by run-pixels.mjs.
gates.claims_to_protect: That a clip reads as its worst over two capture sizes and two scales (RL-209).
gates.actually_tests: Takes the largest value of each number across the readings and re-applies the combined rule. AI-seed clips are read once at 960x540 full size, and the other readings are added only from a primary or red count of 2.5.
gates.vacuous_pass: Because of that staging, a seed clip under 2.5 at 960x540 is never read at 1024x768, where the content differs because the UI scales with the window.
gates.ran_recently: Its self-test passed in my run today.
gates.verdict_reason: Correct worst-of logic. The staging is a cost trade-off, accepted on the record.

gates.name: Margins and sources diagnostic (margins.mjs)
gates.trigger: Run by hand and inside interim-run.sh. It feeds run-table's 'who caused it' column.
gates.claims_to_protect: How much room each counted change has over the area threshold, and whether the HUD, the camera or the world caused it.
gates.actually_tests: Divides each change's window pixels by a hard-coded 21,824 and tests HUD boxes given in 1024x768 coordinates. It ignores the analysis's own thresholdPx.
gates.vacuous_pass: For readings at 960x540 (threshold 14,400 px) or downscaled (3,600 px at 480x270), it understates each change's size by a third up to six times, so real flashes look marginal or under the threshold.
gates.ran_recently: Unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: Use r.thresholdPx and scale the HUD boxes to the frame.

gates.name: Hit windows diagnostic (hit-windows.js)
gates.trigger: Run by hand.
gates.claims_to_protect: Whether one source's flash (body_hit by default) reaches the area test, in measured pixels.
gates.actually_tests: For each granted register row of that source, takes the largest window count in the ticks just after it, against the analysis's own thresholdPx.
gates.vacuous_pass: Changes under an eighth of the threshold read 0, which is fine for the question it answers.
gates.false_alarm: It attributes any change in the window after a grant to that source.
gates.ran_recently: Unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: A small, correct diagnostic.

gates.name: Analyser, recount and staging-drift self-test (selftest.js)
gates.trigger: A step in the CI flash job (ci.yml:117-118), or by hand.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the analyser and the recount give known answers, and that the two copies of the staging have not drifted apart.
gates.actually_tests: 95 checks on synthetic frames, synthetic logs and GIFs, plus a text comparison of functions in flash_worst.gd and render/tools/flash_capture.gd.
gates.vacuous_pass: It has no case with concurrent opposite-direction regions, so the tie defect goes unseen. The check at selftest.js:291 passes whenever worstBig is 4, even if the run passes.
gates.false_alarm: The text-level drift comparison can fail on harmless formatting changes.
gates.ran_recently: Passed when I ran it today. CI last ran it on 2026-11-05.
gates.verdict_reason: A good test. Add the counter-phase case and fix the weak assertion.

gates.name: Pixel pipeline self-test (pixel-selftest.mjs + mock-page)
gates.trigger: The CI flash job, with --require-browser.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the capture driver and the analyser work end to end in a real browser.
gates.actually_tests: Six canvas scenes on a mock page (steady, full-frame strobes at 3 and 4 a second, a small and a large corner strobe, red against grey) are captured and checked against known answers.
gates.vacuous_pass: Says nothing about the game's capture hook, its staging or its rendering.
gates.false_alarm: A flaky browser launch, retried once.
gates.ran_recently: CI last ran it on 2026-11-05. I did not run it (no browser allowed).
gates.verdict_reason: The right end-to-end smoke test for the tool chain.

gates.name: Pipeline logic self-tests (release-pass, nightly, readings, signature-gate, run-pixels, compare-frames, clip-id, head-export)
gates.where: tools/flash/release-pass-selftest.mjs; nightly-selftest.mjs; readings-selftest.mjs; signature-gate-selftest.mjs; run-pixels-selftest.mjs; compare-frames-selftest.mjs; clip-id-selftest.mjs; head-export-selftest.mjs; .github/workflows/ci.yml:119-154
gates.trigger: Steps in the CI flash job.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the rules making a pass stale, the nightly trigger, the four readings and the record writers behave as designed.
gates.actually_tests: Unit tests on throwaway git repositories, stand-in capture and analysis scripts, and synthetic summaries.
gates.vacuous_pass: They confirm the rules are coded as written, including the 3.5 owner limit and the grandfathering. They cannot say whether those rules protect anyone.
gates.upkeep: Medium: many tests to keep in step with policy changes.
gates.ran_recently: I ran seven today and all passed (clip-id needs a browser and was not run). CI last ran them on 2026-11-05.
gates.verdict_reason: Cheap, and they do what they say.

gates.name: Flash pixels dry run workflow (flash-pixels-dryrun.yml)
gates.trigger: workflow_dispatch only.
gates.claims_to_protect: Nothing: it describes itself as a speed measurement, not a check.
gates.actually_tests: Exports HEAD, captures one scenario for N ticks with software rendering, and analyses it with '|| true', so a flash can never fail the job (line 67).
gates.vacuous_pass: By design it cannot fail on a flash.
gates.upkeep: Its pinned action SHAs need bumping alongside ci.yml.
gates.ran_recently: Once, on 2026-10-06 (gh run 37520705360, success).
gates.verdict_reason: Its one-time measurement is done. Fold any future runner pixel job into a real gate.

gates.name: AI seed scan (seed_scan.gd)
gates.trigger: Run by hand. It feeds pick-seeds.mjs.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the chosen AI seeds show each fighter's signature, clashes, transformations and collapses.
gates.actually_tests: Runs the sim alone, with no rendering, and prints counts of signatures, beam outcomes, transformations and building falls per seed, using the same form and tier changes as flash_worst's ai case.
gates.vacuous_pass: It is not a check. Seeds are picked by events, not by how bright they look, so the set can miss the worst visuals (seed-history.json:3-36 lists failing seeds found later).
gates.ran_recently: Unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: A seed-picking tool. It needs no gate of its own.

gates.name: Runtime flash register (VfxFlashRegistry)
gates.trigger: Every tick of the shipped game.
gates.claims_to_protect: That every full flash asks before it draws, with at most 2.5 weight (1.0 reduced) a second, caps on big and total flashes, and nothing red.
gates.actually_tests: Grants or refuses asks from VFX, Rendering (beam, clash, body hit, head, guard, cue flare) and Camera, using each caller's own area, step and colour estimates. A refused flash draws a fallback.
gates.vacuous_pass: It cannot see anything that does not ask, such as scenery sweeping past a moving camera or whole-screen changes (its own header, flash_registry.gd:24-25). Red is judged from the colour the caller passes, which defaults to white.
gates.false_alarm: It can refuse harmless effects, which costs looks, not safety.
gates.upkeep: Medium: every new flash source must ask, with honest area numbers.
gates.ran_recently: Active in every build, including the live pin and the LAN builds.
gates.verdict_reason: The real shipped mitigation, alongside the Reduce flashing lock. Its blind spot, camera and scenery, is where the recorded failures came from (seed-history.json:3-36).

gates.name: Register through the real scene (render/tools/flash_reg_check.gd)
gates.trigger: Local only, in the EP's render-gates.sh. No workflow runs it.
gates.claims_to_protect: That all of Rendering's flashes ask the register, and that its limits hold in real AI matches, a close brawl and reduced mode.
gates.actually_tests: Runs the headless main scene through three 3,600-tick AI matches and staged scenes, and asserts the register's limits, the body-tint rates and the reduced-mode behaviour.
gates.vacuous_pass: Like the CI count, it checks the register's own bookkeeping, not pixels.
gates.ran_recently: Unknown (local only).
gates.verdict_reason: It overlaps the CI count. Merging it into the CI flash job would give it a recorded run.

gates.name: VFX register unit section (effects_check.gd _flashes)
gates.trigger: A local VFX check. No workflow runs it.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the register's rule works: the budget, the low-priority share, red refused, reduced mode.
gates.actually_tests: Sends synthetic asks to a fresh register object.
gates.vacuous_pass: It asserts that six body-hit flashes a second are granted (effects_check.gd:4948-4951). That confirms policy, not safety.
gates.ran_recently: Unknown.
gates.verdict_reason: A cheap unit test of the limiter.

gates.name: Interim site flash checks (check-site-interim.mjs)
gates.trigger: The CI site job, which deploy needs.
gates.claims_to_protect: That the public /play/ carries Legal's flash notice word for word, does not autoplay, and ships Reduce flashing on and locked.
gates.actually_tests: Reads the built site and the pinned tree: the notice text, the options default, features.lock_reduce_flashing, the interim expiry (2026-11-15 under the owner) and the signature gate.
gates.vacuous_pass: It checks words and flags, not pixels. Under the owner interim the pass file is read for the report only (lines 74, 87).
gates.upkeep: Medium: its fixed strings must follow Legal's wording.
gates.ran_recently: CI last ran it on 2026-11-05, for the deploy that is live now. Not since.
gates.verdict_reason: It guards the notice and the lock, which are the mitigations actually live.

gates.name: Clip kit GIF flash label (tools/clips/make.mjs)
gates.trigger: Every clip-kit run that makes a GIF.
gates.claims_to_protect: That clips made for people carry a flash verdict.
gates.actually_tests: Runs analyseGif in-process and writes PASS, OVER GATE or FAIL into index.txt. Nothing stops a failing clip.
gates.vacuous_pass: An analysis error becomes 'CHECK' rather than FAIL, and WebM or PNG clips get no check at all (make.mjs:121-126,248).
gates.ran_recently: Unknown. The code comment is dated 2026-11-07.

gates.claims_to_protect: That HUD elements such as the beat ring switch on at most twice a second, ramp over 0.1 s and hold steady under Reduce flashing (RL-248).
gates.actually_tests: Drives the HUD headless and counts switch-ons and ramp time for the named widgets.

gates.upkeep: Medium: it sits in a 10,453-line file.

The CI flash count cannot fail on real gameplay: the register enforces the same limits check-log.js recounts, and no shipped code calls the unrefusable note() (git grep this run). It is a test of the register's bookkeeping and scenario coverage, not of the screen.

With unequal or jittered regions it reads correctly (7.5 to 10), so it is narrow, at the tie-break in wcag.js:272-274.
